sections.title: Why shadow-board photo + paper sign-out fails FAA / AS9100D / NAS 412 FOD audit
bullets: FAA AC 120-72B human-factors + 14 CFR Part 145 §145.211(c)(1)(vi) quality-control tool-control obligation expect demonstrated pre-close-out tool accountability. Shadow-board photographs and paper sign-out logs do not demonstrate real-time tool location, and FAA Flight Standards + EASA Part-145 audits regularly cite the gap between shadow-board intent and actual per-tool custody state.

AS9100D §8.1.3 + AS9146 + NAS 412 require a documented FOD prevention programme — pre-task / post-task tool counts, sensitive-area tool control, FOD walks. Paper systems cannot sustain that across shift changes or across the 2,000-10,000 tools in a typical heavy-maintenance hangar or OEM production bay.

Boeing D6-1276 + D1-4426 + Airbus AP2633 customer tool-control supplements to AS9100D require evidence of pre-close-out tool reconciliation against the defined kit. Manual reconciliation against a Snap-on ATC / Stanley Vidmar / Lista shadow-board photograph is untenable on high-volume commercial widebody lines and composite assembly cells.

Military depot tool control per AFI 21-101 CAnn Annex + NAVAIR 13-1-6.7 + TM 1-1500-204-23-1 + DA PAM 738-751 + MIL-STD-1530D ASIP demands 100% pre/post-shift tool count on CTK (Consolidated Tool Kit) / FOD-critical / sensitive-item families. Paper-count is the single largest source of QA findings in an USAF / USN / USMC / USA depot maintenance inspection.

Calibration compliance under ISO/IEC 17025 + ANSI/NCSL Z540.3 + NAS 9300 precision measuring equipment + MIL-STD-45662A expects a verifiable calibration interval per instrument. A torque wrench or micrometer in use past its calibration date is a product-escape trigger in aerospace, nuclear and medical device manufacturing.

faq.question: Does the tag satisfy AS9100D §8.1.3 + AS9146 + NAS 412 FOD expectations?
faq.answer: Yes. The tag housing is NAS 412 + AS9146 §7 material-shed-free — no ring, chip or flake is generated in normal use, and epoxy potting per 3M DP-110 / Loctite EA 9460 survives drop / parts-washer / solvent exposure. The programme produces the pre-task and post-task tool inventory record that AS9146 §9 requires, the pre-close-out panel reconciliation that Boeing D6-1276 and Airbus AP2633 expect, and the evidentiary event stream that FAA AC 120-72B + 14 CFR Part 145 §145.211(c)(1)(vi) + AS9100D §8.1.3 audits resolve against.

faq.question: How does it integrate with Snap-on ATC / Stanley Vidmar / Lista / CribMaster / ToolHound / ToolWatch?
faq.answer: The tool master exports from the tool-crib platform are used to build the per-tool GIAI-96 + OEM part-number + calibration-lab reference encoding pack before any tag is cut. At runtime, the smart-crib UHF reader, the shadow-board reader and the zone-portal reader publish EPCIS 2.0 ObjectEvents with bizStep=issuing / returning / calibrating / inspecting / FOD-reconciling which the platform consumes natively. On-tag user memory (UCODE 9 / 9xe) carries last-calibration date + technician assignment + FOD-ledger entry for disconnected flightline / shipyard operation.

faq.question: Will the tag survive parts-washer, Jet-A, Skydrol and daily MRO abuse?
faq.answer: Yes. The polyurethane / silicone / PEEK overmold plus optional 304 / 316L stainless-steel clamp survives Jet-A, MIL-PRF-5606 / MIL-PRF-87257 hydraulic fluid, Skydrol LD-4 / BMS 3-11 phosphate ester, MEK, IPA, acetone, Loctite 243 / 263 / 271 and parts-washer cycles (Safety-Kleen / Graymills). MIL-STD-810H Methods 501 / 502 / 507 / 509 / 510 / 514 / 516 validated; IP67 / IP68; 2 m drop onto concrete validated; UV variant passes ASTM G154 1,000 h for flightline / shipyard deck exposure.

faq.question: How does the programme handle calibration compliance under ISO/IEC 17025 + ANSI/NCSL Z540.3?
faq.answer: Calibration-due-date travels with the tool on the tag (UCODE 9 / 9xe user memory), and EPCIS 2.0 events publish to the calibration-lab system (Fluke MET/TEAM, Beamex CMX, GageTrak, Blue Mountain RAM, IndySoft). The smart-crib door blocks out-of-calibration torque wrenches, micrometers, multimeters and torque drivers from being checked out; out-of-calibration events trigger a re-cal workflow per ISO/IEC 17025:2017 + ANSI/NCSL Z540.1 / Z540.3 + NAS 9300 + MIL-STD-45662A. For aerospace programmes the same cadence engine also enforces AS9100D §7.1.5.2 monitoring and measuring resources.

sources.label: Boeing D6-1276 FOD Program + Airbus AP2633 Foreign Object Damage Prevention Manual
sources.note: OEM tool-control supplements flowing down to Tier-1 / Tier-2 suppliers and MRO partners.

sources.label: AFI 21-101 Aircraft and Equipment Maintenance Management + CAnn Annex Tool Control Program
sources.note: USAF CTK / FOD-critical / sensitive-item pre/post-shift tool count obligation.

sources.label: NAVAIR 13-1-6.7 Tool Control Manual + TM 1-1500-204-23-1 Aeronautical Equipment Maintenance Tool Control
sources.note: USN + USA tool-control obligations governing depot and squadron maintenance tool cribs.

sources.label: ISO/IEC 17025:2017 General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories + ANSI/NCSL Z540.3 Requirements for the Calibration of Measuring and Test Equipment
sources.note: Calibration-laboratory competence and calibration-interval governance flowed through the cadence engine.

sources.label: MIL-STD-130N Change 1 + MIL-STD-1530D Aircraft Structural Integrity Program (ASIP)
sources.note: IUID marking + structural-integrity tool-control basis for government-owned tools used on aircraft structure.

sources.label: GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0 + EPCIS 2.0 (GIAI-96 identifier and event schema) + NXP AN12196 NTAG424 DNA SUN CMAC AES-128
sources.note: Defines the GIAI-96 carrier and the NTAG424 DNA per-scan signature mechanism used on Tier-1 programmes.
